services.processTitle: From tangled tools to one system
services.processSub: The same five-step process whether I'm untangling your CRM or building the automation layer behind it.

processSteps.title: Audit
processSteps.desc: I map every tool, spreadsheet, and manual step currently in use: where leads come in, how they're tracked, and where things tend to break or get missed.

processSteps.title: Design the system
processSteps.desc: From that map, I design the automations and integrations that replace the manual work: what connects to what, what triggers what, and what a human should still review by hand.

processSteps.title: Build & connect
processSteps.desc: I wire it together, GoHighLevel, Zapier, Airtable, Kickserv, Stripe, custom webhooks, whatever the stack calls for, tested against real data before it touches your live pipeline.

processSteps.title: Launch & train
processSteps.desc: The system goes live with documentation your team can actually follow, plus hands-on onboarding so everyone knows what changed and why.

processSteps.title: Support & optimize
processSteps.desc: Systems drift as a business grows. I keep monitoring what I built, fix what breaks, and look for the next manual step worth automating.

about.heroTitle: I've run the systems, not just installed them.
about.intro: I'm Nicolás Mastromarino, an automation architect working with CRM and marketing-operations systems since 2016: first as an SEO analyst, then running email marketing and automation for agency clients, and for the past several years as the person actually operating CRM and dispatch systems inside a growing field-service business.
about.body1Title: What I actually do all day
about.body1: Most of my work isn't glamorous: it's making sure a lead that comes in on a Tuesday shows up correctly in the CRM, gets assigned to the right rep, triggers the right follow-up, and eventually turns into an invoice and a report someone can trust. I build that in GoHighLevel, connect it to tools like Kickserv, Airtable, Stripe, and Google Sheets with Zapier, and then (this is the part most consultants skip) I keep it running as the business changes.
about.body2: GoHighLevel is where I have the deepest hands-on experience, but the actual skill is the same regardless of platform: mapping how a business really runs, then building the CRM and automations around that reality instead of forcing the business to adapt to generic software.
about.body3: Home-services and field-service businesses juggling dispatch, invoicing, and a sales team; agencies who need a hands-on specialist to subcontract CRM and automation work to; and coaches, course creators, and personal brands running everything through funnels and email sequences.

items.title: Dispatch, invoicing, and CRM, finally in sync
items.context: A field-service business running install and repair crews had sales in one tool, dispatch in another, and invoicing in a third, with someone manually re-typing information between all of them every day.
items.work: Rebuilt the CRM in GoHighLevel as the single source of truth, then wired it to the dispatch platform, Airtable, Stripe, and Google Sheets with Zapier so a job moves from lead to invoice without anyone touching a keyboard in between.
items.outcome: What used to be a daily block of manual data entry now happens automatically. The team spends that time on customers instead of re-typing the same job three times.

items.title: A support-ticket system built from nothing
items.context: Customer support requests were arriving by phone, text, and email with no central place to track them, so requests got lost and nobody had visibility into response times.
items.work: Designed and launched a full ticketing system using custom webhooks, Zapier, and CRM automations. Every request creates a ticket, notifies the right person, and gets tracked until it's closed.
items.outcome: Support requests stopped falling through the cracks, and leadership got, for the first time, a real picture of ticket volume and response time.

items.title: Sales reporting leadership could actually trust
items.context: Sales and revenue numbers lived in disconnected spreadsheets that were updated inconsistently, so leadership couldn't get a straight answer on how a rep, or the business, was actually trending.
items.work: Built connected reporting pulling directly from the CRM: daily revenue by rep, multi-year sales trends, and KPI dashboards leadership could open any morning without asking anyone to compile it.
items.outcome: Reporting turned from a monthly scramble into something leadership checks like a dashboard: accurate, current, and no longer dependent on one person's spreadsheet.

items.title: Email automation and CRM for an agency's client base
items.context: An agency needed lead management and email marketing that could scale across many client accounts without rebuilding the wiring from scratch every time.
items.work: Built reusable Zapier workflows connecting the CRM to email marketing automation, along with A/B-tested nurture sequences and the reporting to show which campaigns actually moved the needle.
items.outcome: New client accounts could be onboarded onto proven automation instead of custom work every time, and campaign performance became something the agency could show clients with real numbers.
